skill.name: clerk-auth
skill.description: Provides Clerk authentication patterns for Next.js apps, including provider setup, route protection, server authentication, organizations, webhooks, and user sync.
skill.summary: Guides Clerk authentication setup and route protection for Next.js applications.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: No static security findings were reported for this prompt-only skill. Manual review of SKILL.md found Clerk authentication guidance without executable code, network access, secret access, or prompt injection attempts.

content.value_statement: Clerk setup can be error-prone across middleware, server components, organizations, and webhooks. This skill provides focused implementation guidance for secure Next.js authentication flows.
actual_capabilities: Explains ClerkProvider setup for Next.js App Router applications.
Guides route protection with clerkMiddleware and createRouteMatcher.
Describes server component authentication with auth() and currentUser().
Identifies key Clerk session values, including userId, sessionId, orgId, and claims.
Highlights authentication areas such as organizations, webhooks, and user sync.
limitations: Does not include runnable source code or tests.
Does not replace current Clerk documentation for version-specific API changes.
Does not audit an existing application for security defects.
Provides general patterns, not a complete production architecture.

use_cases.title: Add Clerk to a New Next.js App
use_cases.description: Plan provider setup, sign-in pages, sign-up pages, and user menu placement for a new application.

use_cases.title: Protect Application Routes
use_cases.description: Design middleware rules for public pages, private dashboards, and route groups that require active sessions.

use_cases.title: Review Auth Integration Choices
use_cases.description: Check whether server components, session claims, organizations, and user sync flows are being used consistently.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Clerk Basics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new App Router project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add Clerk authentication to a Next.js App Router project. Include provider placement, sign-in pages, sign-up pages, and required environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Protect Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Clerk middleware rules for my Next.js app. Public routes are home, pricing, and docs. Protected routes are dashboard, settings, and billing.

prompt_templates.title: Use Server Auth State
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to use Clerk auth state in server components. Explain when to use auth(), currentUser(), userId, sessionId, orgId, and claims.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Clerk Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a planned production flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Clerk authentication plan for risks and missing pieces. Cover middleware, organizations, webhooks, user sync, and server-side authorization.

output_examples.input: I need Clerk auth for a new Next.js dashboard.
output_examples.output: A setup checklist covering provider placement, environment variables, sign-in routes, sign-up routes, user menu placement, and protected dashboard routes.

output_examples.input: My dashboard routes should require a signed-in user.
output_examples.output: A middleware plan that separates public pages from private route groups and applies explicit protection to dashboard areas.

output_examples.input: I need to use organization membership in server components.
output_examples.output: Guidance on reading authenticated user context, checking organization identifiers, and keeping authorization checks on the server.

best_practices: Keep all route protection rules centralized in one middleware file.
Use server-side authorization checks for sensitive data access.
Verify Clerk API behavior against current official documentation.
anti_patterns: Relying only on client UI state to protect private data.
Scattering authentication checks across unrelated files without a clear policy.
Assuming organization membership equals permission for every protected action.

faq.question: Does this skill install Clerk packages?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance only. You still install and configure packages in your project.

faq.question: Can it help with Next.js App Router?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill focuses on Clerk patterns for Next.js 14 and 15 App Router projects.

faq.question: Does it cover middleware route protection?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains clerkMiddleware, route matching, and explicit protection for private routes.

faq.question: Can it help with server components?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes using auth() and currentUser() to read authenticated state on the server.

faq.question: Does it include webhook implementation details?
faq.answer: It can guide webhook planning, but it does not provide a complete webhook service implementation.

faq.question: Is it safe for marketplace publication?
faq.answer: The reviewed skill is prompt-only and contains no executable code or suspicious instructions.
